newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty dips vs basket in light dollar-buying.
newsitem.headline: Zloty dips vs basket in light dollar-buying.

text.p: The Polish zloty weakened against the currency basket after a day of relatively live trade spent tracking dollar/mark moves with some early currency-buying, dealers said.

They said there were some client-based currency-buying orders when the zloty temporary its intraday high of 1.85 percent from the parity rate, but client interest faded and the zloty was left to trail dollar/mark for the rest of the day.
"Bids for dollars at 1.85 percent from parity were rather of client origin than speculation," a dealer at a foreign bank in Warsaw said.
The zloty closed at 1.78/1.75 percent from the trading band centre against Wednesday's close at 1.92/1.82 percent.
It closed at 2.8210/25 to the dollar, down from 2.8150/80 on Wednesday and at 1.8531/36 to the mark, down from 1.8505/25.
Overnight rates were quoted above 19 percent for the second day in a row signalling stability around the market's main 14 day drainage rate of 19.14 percent, dealers said.

O/N rates closed flat at opening's levels of 19.10/19.25 percent. Tomorrow/next were at 19.00/19.25 percent, down from 19.20/19.30 percent as banks did not want to keep cash for the weekend, the last in this month's reserve account.
The secondary T-bill market found equilibrium amid thin trade on Tuesday. Foreigners remained on the sidelines, which added to price stability, dealers said.

The focus was on rare trades on the shorter-end of the yield curve, like 50-day to maturity papers. The longest 52-week paper was quoted flat at 19.46/19.40 percent against the last primary yield of 19.46 percent.
Two-year 16-percent bonds, maturing February 1999 were offered around 20.0 percent against maximum yield of 20.20 percent at the last primary tender on October 17.
